title: John the Baptist
lead: John son of Zechariah, a Jewish prophet who preached repentance and baptized people in the Jordan River around AD 28, baptized Jesus, and was executed by Herod Antipas. The Gospels present him as the forerunner who prepares the way for the Lord; Josephus also describes him.

sections.b: Josephus (Jewish Antiquities 18.116–119) calls John "a good man" who urged Jews to practice virtue, justice toward one another and devotion to God, and to come together by baptism, not to win pardon for sins but to purify the body once the soul had already been cleansed by right behavior. Herod Antipas, afraid that John's influence over the crowds might lead to a revolt, had him executed at the fortress of Machaerus. Many readers in Josephus's day thought Antipas's defeat by the Nabatean king Aretas was God's punishment for it.
